preconditions: filename is null or points to a readable null-terminated byte string.
this identifies writable storage for every recovered offset; the capacity of the filename buffer beginning at 0x14 is not established.
postconditions: Returns -1 immediately when filename is null or empty.
Returns -2 after logging when neither the direct path nor any registered fallback path can be opened.
Returns -1 after closing and logging when the 12-byte header matches none of the three recovered literals or allocation fails.

On success returns 0, retains the open handle at 0x10, stores three read dwords at 0x114, 0x118, and 0x120, stores an allocated payload pointer at 0x128, and sets 0x11C to (value at 0x118 shifted left 8) plus 24.
side_effects: Copies filename without an explicit bound to the object buffer at 0x14 and invokes a path-preparation runtime helper.
Performs synchronous file open, read, and close operations through compiler-runtime wrappers.
Reads the fallback path registry count at 0x008B8E30 and entries at 0x008B5A3C with stride 132.
Allocates a payload buffer through a compiler-runtime allocation wrapper.

external_dependencies.name: compiler-runtime path preparation, file I/O, string comparison/formatting, and allocation wrappers

unresolved: The object type and semantic names of the header fields are not established.
The filename buffer capacity, maximum registry count, registry ownership, and allocation-size overflow behavior are unknown.
Read counts and return values are not checked in the recovered body; short-read behavior is unknown.
Successful ownership and later release of the retained handle and payload require downstream contracts.
The thiscall and int-shaped pointer types are raw decompiler evidence and have not reached ABI_REVIEWED.
tests_required: Unit: null and empty filenames return -1 without object writes.
Unit: direct-open and fallback-open success paths populate the exact recovered fields.
Unit: open, header, and allocation failures return the recovered codes and perform the recovered close/log actions.
Negative: bound filename and registry traversal and guard the shifted allocation size before implementation.
Integration: define later handle/payload teardown before code generation.
